title: Performance Optimization
objectives: Avoid jank by keeping the main thread free

sections.markdown: Android performance is about rendering each frame within ~16ms (60fps), using memory efficiently, and starting fast. Dropped frames ('jank') usually mean the main thread is doing too much.

The classic Android leak: holding an Activity Context in a static field or a long-lived singleton. The Activity can't be GC'd after it's destroyed. Use the application Context for long-lived needs and detect leaks with LeakCanary.
Loading full-resolution bitmaps into small ImageViews — a leading cause of OOM. Downsample (inSampleSize) or use an image library (Glide/Coil) that handles sizing and caching.
Measure before optimizing. Use Android Studio Profiler (CPU/Memory/Network), Layout Inspector for overdraw, Macrobenchmark for startup, and LeakCanary for leaks.

flashcards.back: ~16ms per frame; exceeding it drops frames (jank).
Holding an Activity Context/View in a static or long-lived object.
Full-res images in small views waste memory and cause OOM; downsample or use Glide/Coil.
